{"prompt":"You are the first worker in a C-to-Rust translation project. Your task is a BRAINSTORM: do NOT write any code yet.

The source is a small, dependency-free C implementation of TOTP (time-based one-time passwords) located in the workspace. Read these files:
- totp.h, totp.c (core algorithms: sha1, hmac_sha1, hotp, totp, from_base32, plus inline helpers unpack32/unpack64/pack32/rotl)
- std.h, std.c (freestanding libc shims: memset/memcpy/strlen)
- main.c (CLI)
- test.c (unit tests: test_pack, test_sha1, test_hmac_sha1, test_hotp, test_from_base32)
- Makefile, README.md, LICENSE.md

Then write a file called `plan.md` in the workspace root containing:
1. A short strategy for translating this C codebase to Rust (crate layout, module structure, how to map the C API to Rust idioms, how to handle the NO_STD/freestanding std.c shims, how to handle the CLI main.c, and how to port test.c into a Rust test suite).
2. A list of the core difficulties and candidate approaches (e.g. the `__attribute__((visibility))` export macro, the clobbered-buffer sha1 signature with len/cap, the base32 return-value semantics, integer overflow handling, the inline static functions in the header).
3. A recommended crate structure (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, src/totp.rs, src/std.rs, tests/).

Also create `tasks.json` in the workspace root containing 3 to 6 seed tasks in this JSON format (an array of objects with "id", "title", "status" fields, all status "pending"):
[
  {"id": 1, "title": "...", "status": "pending"},
  ...
]

The seed tasks should cover: (a) set up Cargo project skeleton (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs), (b) port totp.h + totp.c to Rust (sha1, hmac_sha1, hotp, totp, from_base32, helpers), (c) port std.c/std.h shims if needed, (d) port main.c to a Rust binary, (e) port test.c to a Rust test suite, (f) build and run tests until green.

Keep plan.md concise but concrete. Do not write any Rust code files yet. When done, report what you wrote."}
